title: Convert fractional resource budgets to integer allocation geometry at the consumer boundary
applies_when: A host_size, cache capacity or memory-budget lead treats a floating-point GB share as a tensor shape, or proposes integer coercion before inspecting the budget's units and its final allocation consumer.
lesson: Follow the unit conversion, not just the annotation. SGLang splits hicache_size into proportional floating-point GB budgets; HostKVCache and MambaPoolHost convert each positive budget with int(host_size * 1e9 // size_per_token) before deriving integer token/page geometry. A fractional budget is not itself an invalid shape. Coercing the GB share to int earlier can turn a positive sub-GB budget into zero and select the ratio-based sizing branch instead. Inspect the last budget-to-bytes-to-elements conversion, then test fractional shares and a normal control before investing in an allocator environment or a type repair.
avoid_when: Units may be bytes, GiB, tokens or pages in another API; do not assume this GB conversion. Fractional rounding, page alignment, aggregate over-budget allocation, zero-byte denominators, distributed minimum-capacity synchronization and mixed-pool invariants still need their own reachable tests. Source and extracted arithmetic refute the integer-only premise here, not native SGLang initialization, QSA draft compatibility, memory safety, performance or every caller.

evidence.note: _split_hicache_size returns proportional float shares; build_kv_host_pool explicitly accepts Optional[float]. These are budgets, not tensor dimensions.
Positive fixed GB sizing is converted to an integer token capacity before page alignment; nonpositive host_size selects ratio-based sizing. Source contract, not native/distributed qualification.
Mamba host allocation uses the same GB-to-integer-token conversion. Its int annotation does not impose an integer-only runtime budget.
Official source examples expect float two/three-pool budget shares. Reading these tests is not a claim that the registered SGLang suite ran.
